title: Standard opens of Proj: basis, intersections, inclusions and coverings
statement:
Let $S= igoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], the set of homogeneous primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq S$ with $S_+
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$; for $f\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree let $D_+(f)=\{\mathfrak p\in X: f
otin\mathfrak p\}$ (a *standard open*), and $S_{(f)}$ the degree-zero part of $S_f$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], with the canonical homeomorphism $D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$. Then: (0) the standard opens form a basis of the topology of $X$, and $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$ for $f,g$ homogeneous of positive degree; (1) for $f,g$ homogeneous of positive degree, $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ if and only if $g^e=af$ for some $e\ge1$ and some homogeneous $a\in S$ (necessarily of degree $e\deg g-\deg f$ when $af
eq0$); in this case $f$ is a unit of $S_g$ and $f^{\deg g}/g^{\deg f}$ is a unit of $S_{(g)}$; (2) every open covering of a standard open $D_+(f)$ can be refined to a finite covering $D_+(f)= igcup_{i=1}^nD_+(g_i)$ by standard opens; (3) for $g_1,\dots,g_n\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree, $D_+(f)\subseteq igcup_iD_+(g_i)$ if and only if the elements $g_i^{\deg f}/f^{\deg g_i}\in S_{(f)}$ generate the unit ideal of $S_{(f)}$.

source.place: Constructions, Section 01M3 (label section-proj), the paragraph before Lemma 01M4 (basis, $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$); Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open) (1)(a),(b), (2), (3) and its proof; Algebra Lemma 00JP (label lemma-topology-proj) for $D_+(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$

proof.text:
*Clause (0): standard opens are open, and intersections.* For $f$ homogeneous of positive degree, $D_+(f)$ is the set $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\in X: f
otin\mathfrak p\}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-spectrum-basic-opens-basis], hence open by (i) of that lemma. For $f,g$ homogeneous of positive degrees $d,k$, the product $fg$ is homogeneous of degree $d+k>0$, and $D_+(fg)=D(fg)=D(f)\cap D(g)=D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)$ by (ii) of that lemma (directly: $fg
otin\mathfrak p$ iff $f
otin\mathfrak p$ and $g
otin\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak p$ being prime).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00JP (label lemma-topology-proj) (1), (2) and their proof

proof.text:
*Clause (0): the standard opens form a basis.* Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $x\in U$ with prime $\mathfrak p$. By (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-spectrum-basic-opens-basis] there is $r\in S$ with $x\in D(r)\subseteq U$; write $r=\sum_ir_i$, $r_i\in S_i$; by (iii) of that lemma $x\in D(r_i)\subseteq D(r)$ for some $i$. If $i\ge1$, $D(r_i)=D_+(r_i)$ is a standard open with $x\in D_+(r_i)\subseteq U$. If $i=0$: since $S_+
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$, some $s\in S_+$ is not in $\mathfrak p$; $s$ is the sum of its homogeneous components, all of positive degree, and $\mathfrak p$ is an ideal, so some homogeneous $h$ of positive degree has $h
otin\mathfrak p$. Then $r_0h
otin\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak p$ prime), $r_0h$ is homogeneous of degree $\deg h>0$, and $D_+(r_0h)=D(r_0)\cap D(h)\subseteq D(r_0)$ by (ii) of that lemma; so $x\in D_+(r_0h)\subseteq U$. Hence every open set is a union of standard opens, and with step 1 the standard opens form a basis of the topology of $X$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00JP (label lemma-topology-proj) (3), (4), (5) and their proof

proof.text: *Clause (1), forward: the unit of $S_{(g)}$.* Let $f,g$ be homogeneous of positive degrees $d=\deg f$, $k=\deg g$, with $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$. Let $\iota_g:\operatorname{Spec}S_{(g)}\to X$ be the open immersion with image $D_+(g)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] (the homeomorphism $D_+(g)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(g)}$ of Algebra 00JP (6)); by that lemma (with the roles of $f,g$ exchanged) $\iota_g^{-1}(D_+(f))=D(f^k/g^d)$, the principal open of $u=f^k/g^d\in S_{(g)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Since the image $D_+(g)$ of $\iota_g$ is contained in $D_+(f)$, $\iota_g^{-1}(D_+(f))$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(g)}$, i.e. $D(u)=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(g)}$: $u$ lies in no prime ideal of $S_{(g)}$. By (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], $u=f^{\deg g}/g^{\deg f}$ is a unit of $S_{(g)}$.

source.place: Constructions, proof of Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open), first paragraph, proof of (1)(a); Algebra, Lemma 00JP (label lemma-topology-proj) (6) and Lemma 00E0 (label lemma-Zariski-topology)

proof.text: *Clause (1), forward: $f$ is a unit of $S_g$ and the homogeneous witness.* Keep the notation of step 3 and let $v\in S_{(g)}$ with $uv=1$. In $S_g$ (which contains $S_{(g)}$ as the subring of degree-zero fractions [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]) we have $f\cdot(f^{k-1}v/g^d)=f^kv/g^d=uv=1$ ($k\ge1$), so $f$ is a unit of $S_g$. Write its inverse as $b/g^n$ with $b\in S$, $n\ge0$; replacing $(b,n)$ by $(bg^t,n+t)$ for large $t$ we may assume $n\ge1$ and $nk\ge d$. Then $fb/g^n=1$ in $S_g$ means $g^N(fb-g^n)=0$ in $S$ for some $N\ge0$, i.e. $g^Nfb=g^{N+n}$. Let $a_0$ be the homogeneous component of $b$ of degree $nk-d$. Since $g^N$ and $f$ are homogeneous, the component of degree $(N+n)k$ of $g^Nfb$ is $g^Nfa_0$, while $g^{N+n}$ is homogeneous of degree $(N+n)k$; comparing components gives $g^Nfa_0=g^{N+n}$. Put $e=N+n\ge1$ and $a=g^Na_0$, homogeneous of degree $ek-d$: then $g^e=af$. (If $af\ne0$, any homogeneous $a$ with $g^e=af$ has degree $e\deg g-\deg f$, by comparing degrees.)

source.place: Constructions, proof of Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open), first paragraph, proof of (1)(a) and (1)(b) ('Write the inverse of $f$ in $S_g$ as $a/g^d$ ... replace $a$ by its homogeneous part ... $g^e=af$')

proof.text: *Clause (1), converse and the unit statements.* Suppose $g^e=af$ with $e\ge1$, $a$ homogeneous. If $\mathfrak p\in D_+(g)$ then $g^e\notin\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak p$ prime), so $f\notin\mathfrak p$ (else $af\in\mathfrak p$): $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$. Units: in $S_g$, $f\cdot a/g^e=g^e/g^e=1$. In $S_{(g)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]: if $af=0$ then $g^e=0$, so $S_g=0=S_{(g)}$ and every element is a unit; otherwise $\deg a=ek-d\ge0$ ($d=\deg f$, $k=\deg g$), $a^k/g^{ek-d}\in S_{(g)}$ (numerator of degree $k(ek-d)$), and $(f^k/g^d)(a^k/g^{ek-d})=(af)^k/g^{ek}=g^{ek}/g^{ek}=1$. So $f$ is a unit of $S_g$ and $f^{\deg g}/g^{\deg f}$ is a unit of $S_{(g)}$; with steps 3 and 4 this proves (1).

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open) (1)(a),(b),(c) and its proof (the map $b/f^n\mapsto a^nb/g^{ne}$)

proof.text: *Clause (2).* Let $f$ be homogeneous of positive degree and $D_+(f)=\bigcup_jU_j$ an open covering. The space $D_+(f)$ is quasi-compact: it is the image of $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ under the continuous map $\iota_f$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], and $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ is quasi-compact by (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. For each $x\in D_+(f)$ choose $j$ with $x\in U_j$; $U_j$ is open in $X$ (as $D_+(f)$ is, step 1), so by the basis property (step 2) there is $h_x$ homogeneous of positive degree with $x\in D_+(h_x)\subseteq U_j$. The open sets $D_+(h_x)$ cover $D_+(f)$, so finitely many $D_+(h_{x_1}),\dots,D_+(h_{x_n})$ do; with $g_i=h_{x_i}$ we get $D_+(f)=\bigcup_{i=1}^nD_+(g_i)$ (each $D_+(g_i)\subseteq U_{j}\subseteq D_+(f)$), a finite covering by standard opens refining $(U_j)$.

source.place: Constructions, proof of Lemma 01M4 (label lemma-standard-open), second paragraph (quasi-compactness via Algebra Lemma 00E8, label lemma-quasi-compact, and the basis)

proof.text: *Clause (3).* Let $f$ have degree $d>0$ and $g_1,\dots,g_n$ be homogeneous of positive degrees $k_i$; put $u_i=g_i^{d}/f^{k_i}\in S_{(f)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], $\iota_f^{-1}(D_+(g_i))=D(u_i)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$, hence $\iota_f^{-1}(\bigcup_iD_+(g_i))=\bigcup_iD(u_i)$. Since $\iota_f$ maps $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ onto $D_+(f)$, $D_+(f)\subseteq\bigcup_iD_+(g_i)$ iff $\iota_f^{-1}(\bigcup_iD_+(g_i))=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$ iff $\bigcup_iD(u_i)=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(f)}$, and by (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] this holds iff $u_1,\dots,u_n$ generate the unit ideal of $S_{(f)}$.
